podcast.title: Major Label Debut
podcast.body: Released on June 17, 1997, as the band's first record with MCA. The recording process was rushed, complicated by drummer Scott Rainer's broken heels and Mark Hoppas's strained voice. MCA executives were initially hesitant about the album's "punk thing" and "goofy sense of humor," but it eventually sold half a million copies within a year after the single "Dammit" gained radio promotion. "The record was called Dude Ranch. And to be honest, the people at MCA weren't crazy about this record."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 1

podcast.body: This album marked Blink-182's breakthrough into the mainstream music scene. The band notably showcased this record while performing on the Warped Tour. "They came out of San Diego and had a mainstream breakthrough with their dude ranch album, a record that they put on display when they went on the road with the warp tour."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
